text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bre-X's woes panic markets: Confidence rocked by acknowledgement of 'strong possibility' estimates overstated.
- IRA blamed for bombs on tracks: Manchester blasts seen as warning.
- 39 bodies found in California house: Cult death plot suspected.
- Police worry youths were dead: Poses in seized photos could lead to digging in back yard.
- Cancelled visits stir election rumour mill: Presidents of Phillipines, Ireland, change plans after Ottawa tells them May is opportune time.
- Bre-X panic hits markets: Junior mining shares battered over fears that Busang gold find reserve estimates may have been overstated.
- U.S. vultures grab Eaton's bank debt: Scotiabank, TD sell C$160 million owed.
- Black abandons quest to control Financial Post: Media giant ponders starting national paper instead.
- Avenor-Repap merger defeated: Future clouded as Avenor investors vote 3-1 against deal.
- Disaster for Bre-X: Investment community reels on news that Busang, heralded as one of the biggest gold finds in history, may contain no mineable gold.
- Avenor in play as Repap deal folds.
